literal: One day like seven days passes, to those who pine, reckoning the coming day of him who went to a far distance.
translation: To those who pine, counting the days until the return of their beloved who has gone to a far country, a single day feels as long as seven.
modern: தொலைதூரத்திற்குச் சென்ற காதலர் திரும்பி வரும் நாளைக் கணக்கிட்டு ஏங்குபவர்களுக்கு, ஒரு நாள் என்பது ஏழு நாட்களைப் போல மெதுவாகக் கழியும்.
explanation: This couplet beautifully captures the agonizingly slow passage of time experienced by a pining lover. The speaker waits for her partner who has traveled to a distant land, constantly counting down the days until his promised return. In this state of intense longing, each single day feels as long as a whole week of seven days. The poet uses the simple contrast between 'one day' and 'seven days' to measure the psychological weight of separation.
